title: Warranty for Houses and Construction Works 2026: Periods and Amounts
desc: Construction warranty 2026: at least 24 months for detached houses, 60 for apartments; 3% or 5% retention; penalties for contractors who refuse to repair.
summary: Warranty periods for detached houses, apartments and construction works, retention amounts, how to claim a warranty and the contractor's responsibility under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 207/2026/ND-CP.
body: A new house cracks in the wall or leaks through the ceiling after a few months: who must repair it, and within what time? The answer lies in the warranty rules in Article 64 of the Construction Law 2025, Decree 207/2026/ND-CP and the Housing Law 2023.
1. Who must provide the warranty, and for what?

The construction contractor warrants the part of the work it built; the equipment supplier warrants the equipment it supplied. The warranty covers remedying, repairing and replacing damaged or defective equipment (Clause 1, Article 64 of the Construction Law 2025).

For housing, Clause 3, Article 129 of the Housing Law lists specifically: repair and remedying of damage to the frame, columns, beams, floors, walls, ceilings, roof, terrace, stairs, cladding, tiling, plastering, electrical system, water supply and drainage, water tanks, septic tanks, and remedying of tilting, subsidence, cracking and collapse of the house.
Under Clause 2, Article 129 of the Housing Law, housing is warranted from completion of construction and acceptance for use:
Equipment attached to the house: the manufacturer's period.

Decree 207/2026/ND-CP cross-refers: for housing works, the content and period of warranty follow the housing law (Clause 6, Article 33). For other works using State capital, the period runs from acceptance and is not less than 24 months for special-grade and grade I works and not less than 12 months for other grades; works using other capital may refer to these levels (Clause 5, Article 32).

Under Clause 7, Article 32 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, for works using State capital the minimum warranty retention is 3% of the contract value for special-grade and grade I works and 5% for other grades. Works using other capital (such as a household's house) may refer to these levels.

The homeowner and contractor should state clearly in the contract: the warranty period, warranty amount, form (money retained or bank guarantee) and when it is returned. The contractor gets back the warranty money only after the warranty period ends and the project owner confirms that its responsibilities have been fulfilled (Clause 2, Article 32).
4. Found a defect: how to claim the warranty?
Photograph and record the defect and the date it was found.
Notify the construction contractor and equipment supplier and request warranty service (preferably in writing, or in saved messages).
The contractor must repair defects arising during the warranty period and bear all related costs (Clause 2, Article 33).
The homeowner inspects and accepts the warranty work; when the period ends, confirms completion of the warranty and returns the warranty money if requirements are met.

The contractor may refuse the warranty if the defect is not its fault or is due to force majeure under the contract. If the fault is the contractor's and it does not provide the warranty, the project owner may use the warranty money to hire another party to repair (Clause 3, Article 33). The homeowner must also use and maintain the house in accordance with regulations.
5. What happens to a contractor who fails to provide the warranty?

Under Article 34 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP, a contractor that does not perform its warranty responsibility is fined VND 40–60 million and must provide the warranty; failing to prepare a warranty completion report to send to the project owner is fined VND 20–30 million. These are the fines for organisations; individuals are fined half (Article 5).

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The Housing Law 2023 is currently partially no longer in effect; Article 129 as cited has not been found amended in our library. Warranty periods longer than the minimum may be agreed in the contract.
